updates.topic: TEMPO-2 secondary analysis — the "minor DISABLING stroke" question (the single most important gap)
updates.whatIsNew: Prespecified-style secondary analysis of all 884 TEMPO-2 patients (369 women, 41.7%; median age 72 [IQR 61-80]). Only 100 (11.3%) had disabling and 784 (88.7%) nondisabling deficits by TREAT Task Force consensus. In the DISABLING group, return to baseline mRS at 90 d occurred in 29/53 (54.7%) with tenecteplase vs 32/47 (68.1%) with standard of care: adjusted RR 0.81 (95% CI 0.60-1.10). In the nondisabling group 280 (73.9%) vs 306 (75.6%), aRR 0.98 (95% CI 0.91-1.07); P for interaction = 0.32. Disabling patients presented later (onset-to-treatment 411 vs 278 min). ARAMIS and NINDS definitions of "disabling" were also explored and did not modify the effect. The authors explicitly conclude this "suggests the need to reevaluate thrombolysis in minor disabling stroke" — i.e. it directly challenges the guideline rule the document states as settled (thrombolyse any disabling deficit regardless of NIHSS).
updates.citation: Zhang Y, Buck BH, Barber PA, Chatterjee K, Clarke B, Choi PMC, et al. Thrombolysis with tenecteplase for minor disabling stroke: secondary analysis of the TEMPO-2 randomized clinical trial. JAMA Neurol. 2025;82(12):1243-50. doi:10.1001/jamaneurol.2025.4152.

updates.topic: Pooled RCT evidence: IV thrombolysis in minor stroke (NIHSS ≤5) — the definitive quantitative synthesis
updates.whatIsNew: Meta-analysis restricted to RCTs enrolling only minor stroke (NIHSS ≤5). Primary analysis: 4 RCTs, N = 3,364. IVT vs non-thrombolytic standard of care gave NO improvement in excellent outcome (mRS 0-1 at 90 d: OR 0.85, 95% CI 0.70-1.03), SIGNIFICANTLY LOWER odds of functional independence (mRS 0-2: OR 0.71, 95% CI 0.55-0.91), and higher odds of sICH (OR 5.22, 95% CI 1.76-15.48) and 90-day mortality (OR 2.40, 95% CI 1.23-4.67). Subgroup: no benefit in either disabling (OR 0.84, 95% CI 0.38-1.88) or nondisabling (OR 0.82, 95% CI 0.66-1.03) symptoms. PROSPERO CRD42024621714. This is the strongest single citation available for the document's central claim, and it goes further than the document does (net harm signal, not merely "no benefit").
updates.citation: Doheim MF, Nguyen TN, Xiong Y, Chen HS, Bhatt NR, Wang Y, et al. Meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials on IV thrombolysis in patients with minor acute ischemic stroke. Neurology. 2025;105(3):e213863. doi:10.1212/WNL.0000000000213863.

updates.topic: ARAMIS — DAPT non-inferior to alteplase in minor NON-DISABLING stroke within 4.5 h (the trial that underpins the document's own recommendation, but is never cited)
updates.whatIsNew: Open-label, blinded-endpoint non-inferiority RCT, 38 Chinese hospitals, Oct 2018-Apr 2022; 760 patients with NIHSS ≤5 AND ≤1 point on key single NIHSS items (i.e. non-disabling), randomised within 4.5 h to DAPT (clopidogrel 300 mg then 75 mg + aspirin 100 mg for 12±2 days) vs alteplase 0.9 mg/kg. Median age 64, median NIHSS 2. mRS 0-1 at 90 d: 346/369 (93.8%) DAPT vs 320/350 (91.4%) alteplase; risk difference 2.3% (95% CI -1.5% to 6.2%), lower 1-sided 97.5% CI limit -1.5% vs a -4.5% non-inferiority margin, P for non-inferiority <0.001. sICH 1/371 (0.3%) vs 3/351 (0.9%). NOTE: published 2023, so slightly outside the 2024-2026 frame, but it is the direct randomised basis for "DAPT preferred over lysis in non-disabling deficits" and its absence is a substantive citation gap.
updates.citation: Chen HS, Cui Y, Zhou ZH, Zhang H, Wang LX, Wang WZ, et al. Dual antiplatelet therapy vs alteplase for patients with minor nondisabling acute ischemic stroke: the ARAMIS randomized clinical trial. JAMA. 2023;329(24):2135-44. doi:10.1001/jama.2023.7827.

updates.topic: ARAMIS secondary analysis — NIHSS 0-3 vs 4-5 changes the answer (directly relevant to the document's NIHSS-threshold discussion)
updates.whatIsNew: As-treated analysis of 719 ARAMIS patients split into NIHSS 0-3 (n=585) and NIHSS 4-5 (n=134). mRS 0-1 at 90 d: NIHSS 0-3 — DAPT 277/290 (95.5%) vs alteplase 272/295 (92.2%); NIHSS 4-5 — DAPT 43/52 (82.7%) vs alteplase 74/82 (90.2%). Significant treatment-by-baseline-NIHSS interaction, P = 0.048. No sICH in any DAPT patient; 3 sICH in the alteplase NIHSS 0-3 group and 1 in the NIHSS 4-5 group. Interpretation: DAPT favoured at NIHSS 0-3, alteplase favoured at NIHSS 4-5 — a genuinely new, practice-relevant nuance the document's blanket "NIHSS ≤5 non-disabling → DAPT" statement does not capture.
updates.citation: Fei ZX, Yin Y, Cui Y, Nguyen TN, Chen HS. Dual antiplatelet therapy versus alteplase for mild stroke with admission NIHSS score 0-3 versus 4-5: a secondary analysis of the ARAMIS randomized trial. CNS Drugs. 2025;39(10):1037-46. doi:10.1007/s40263-025-01211-6.

updates.topic: Network meta-analysis: DAPT vs IVT vs aspirin in acute NON-DISABLING minor stroke (ESO-affiliated authors)
updates.whatIsNew: Bayesian random-effects network meta-analysis of 4 RCTs + 2 observational studies (5,897 patients for the primary outcome), NIHSS ≤5 with non-disabling symptoms, treatment started ≤24 h. Versus IVT (alteplase), DAPT (clopidogrel + aspirin) had significantly higher odds of mRS 0-1 at 3 months (OR 1.52, 95% CrI 1.09-2.35); aspirin alone did not (OR 1.36, 95% CrI 0.87-2.30). DAPT also had lower odds of sICH than alteplase (OR 0.14, 95% CrI 0.03-0.91). Treatment ranking for every outcome: DAPT > aspirin > IVT. PROSPERO CRD42024522038.
updates.citation: Lun F, Palaiodimou L, Katsanos AH, Tsivgoulis G, Turc G. Intravenous thrombolysis or antiplatelet therapy for acute nondisabling ischemic stroke: a systematic review and network meta-analysis. Eur Stroke J. 2025;10(2):330-8. doi:10.1177/23969873241293323.

updates.topic: Expert guidance document dedicated to exactly this monograph's topic (disabling vs non-disabling minor stroke)
updates.whatIsNew: Scenario-based framework co-authored by Coutts (TEMPO-2 PI), Fischer, Khatri (PRISMS PI) and colleagues. Key stated positions: minor ischaemic stroke (NIHSS ≤5) accounts for over half of all ischaemic strokes and up to 30% are disabled at 90 days; IVT is preferred for DISABLING symptoms within 4.5 h; DAPT remains standard for non-cardioembolic NON-DISABLING events; for cardioembolic minor stroke ineligible for reperfusion, early anticoagulation within 48 h appears safe and beneficial; evidence for routine EVT in minor stroke with LVO remains limited and controversial. It also explicitly covers rapidly-improving-but-still-disabling symptoms and post-reperfusion antithrombotic strategy — both of which the document discusses without a modern citation.
updates.citation: De Santis F, Foschi M, D'Anna L, Coutts SB, Fischer U, Khatri P, et al. Acute treatment of disabling and nondisabling minor ischemic stroke: expert guidance for clinicians. Stroke. 2026;57(2):549-59. doi:10.1161/STROKEAHA.125.053504.

updates.topic: TEMPO-2 secondary analysis — patients >80 years are harmed
updates.whatIsNew: Post hoc analysis of the 884 ITT patients; 208 (23.5%) were >80 years. Significant age-by-treatment interactions for mRS responder, mRS 0-1, return to baseline, EQ-5D index and recanalisation. In patients >80 y, mRS 0-1 occurred in 49 (46.2%) with tenecteplase vs 61 (59.8%) with control (aRR 0.83, 95% CI 0.72-0.97); in patients ≤80 y, 249 (76.4%) vs 260 (74.7%) (aRR 1.01, 95% CI 0.98-1.03). Recanalisation was more frequent with tenecteplase in BOTH groups (aRR ≤80 y 2.06, 95% CI 1.60-2.65; >80 y 2.77, 95% CI 2.21-3.47), as was NIHSS 0 at 5 d/discharge. Serious adverse events were more frequent with tenecteplase in those >80 y (RR 2.29, 95% CI 1.27-4.13); any extra/intracranial haemorrhage 5 (4.7%) vs 0 (P = 0.026). Class III evidence. The recanalisation-without-benefit dissociation is a strong teaching point for a monograph.
updates.citation: Ganesh A, Vatanpour S, Yu AYX, Barber P, Choi PMC, Field TS, et al. Outcomes after minor ischemic stroke in older patients treated with IV thrombolysis vs standard of care in the TEMPO-2 trial. Neurology. 2026;106(9):e214925. doi:10.1212/WNL.0000000000214925.

updates.topic: TEMPO-2 secondary analysis — recanalisation matters, but tenecteplase still does not
updates.whatIsNew: Observational cohort analysis of the 517/886 (58.3%) TEMPO-2 patients with follow-up CTA at 4-8 h. Successful recanalisation (revised AOL 2b/3) in 178 (34.6%) — 122 (68.5%) tenecteplase vs 56 (31.5%) control — vs 336 (65.4%) unsuccessful. Successful recanalisation was associated with the primary outcome (adjusted RR 1.21, 95% CI 1.07-1.34) and with far less stroke progression (2.8% vs 13.1%; aRR 0.21, 95% CI 0.08-0.52). Tenecteplase was the strongest independent predictor of recanalisation (OR 3.48, 95% CI 2.33-5.18). This is the mechanistic paradox at the heart of TEMPO-2 and is worth an explicit paragraph.
updates.citation: Singh N, Strbian D, Vatanpour S, Field TS, Yu AYX, Ganesh A, et al. Association of successful recanalization and functional outcomes in minor ischemic stroke with proven occlusion: a secondary analysis of TEMPO-2 trial. Stroke. 2026;57(8):2305-14. doi:10.1161/STROKEAHA.125.052872.

updates.topic: TEMPO-2 secondary analysis — haemorrhage patterns explain the mortality signal
updates.whatIsNew: Of 884 participants, 865 had complete 24-h imaging. Any ICH (Heidelberg classification) in 102 (11.8%). Any ICH was NOT associated with reduced odds of returning to baseline function (aOR 0.93, 95% CI 0.87-1.00) but WAS associated with higher 90-day mortality (9.8% vs 1.8%; adjusted HR 3.71, 95% CI 1.54-8.95). Any ICH was more frequent with tenecteplase (14.4% vs 9.2%, P = 0.02), mostly petechial haemorrhagic transformation; symptomatic ICH 8 (1.9%) vs 2 (0.5%), P = 0.06. Directly substantiates the document's brief remark that TEMPO-2 recorded more deaths in the tenecteplase arm.
updates.citation: Massicotte S, Vatanpour S, Doolan C, Zhang J, Ganesh A, Choi PMC, et al. Intracranial hemorrhage patterns and outcomes in minor stroke: analysis of the TEMPO-2 trial. Stroke. 2026;57(6):1526-34. doi:10.1161/STROKEAHA.125.054491.

updates.topic: PUMICE — prourokinase vs standard care in mild stroke (a new negative trial in exactly this population)
updates.whatIsNew: Multicentre open-label blinded-endpoint RCT, 89 Chinese hospitals, Nov 2022-Dec 2023; 1,446 patients with NIHSS ≤5 within 4.5 h (patients intended for EVT excluded). Median age 65.9 y, 65.5% male. Prourokinase 35 mg (15 mg bolus + 20 mg over 30 min) vs standard care. mRS 0-1 at 90 d: 639/723 (88.5%) vs 658/723 (91.0%); RR 0.97 (95% CI 0.94-1.01), P = 0.12. sICH 0.7% (5/723) vs 0%; 90-day mortality 2.3% vs 1.4%. A third distinct lytic agent now fails in minor stroke — strengthens the class-effect argument.
updates.citation: Xiong Y, Meng X, Jin A, Campbell BCV, Xu A, Dong Q, et al. Prourokinase vs standard care for patients with mild ischemic stroke: the PUMICE randomized clinical trial. JAMA Neurol. 2025;82(3):258-66. doi:10.1001/jamaneurol.2024.4688.

updates.topic: TRUST — IV urokinase vs best medical treatment in acute minor stroke (fourth negative lytic trial)
updates.whatIsNew: Multicentre open-label blinded-endpoint RCT, 25 Chinese hospitals, Oct 2020-Feb 2023; 999 patients with NIHSS ≤5 within 6 h. Median age 64, 36.9% women, median NIHSS 3 (IQR 2-4). Urokinase 1,000,000 U vs best medical treatment. mRS 0-1 at 90 d: 427 (84.9%) vs 425 (85.7%); adjusted RR 1.00 (95% CI 0.96-1.05), P = 0.87. sICH within 36 h in 3 (0.6%) vs 1 (0.2%); RR 1.83 (95% CI 0.16-20.27), P = 0.62.
updates.citation: Tao Y, Gao Y, Zhao L, Xu Y, Jiang C, Liu K, et al. Effect of intravenous urokinase vs best medicine treatment on functional outcome for patients with acute minor stroke (TRUST): a randomized controlled trial. BMC Med. 2025;23(1):6. doi:10.1186/s12916-024-03820-2.

updates.topic: ATTEST-2 — tenecteplase non-inferior to alteplase within 4.5 h (the evidence base for the document's own "tenecteplase 0.25 mg/kg or alteplase 0.9 mg/kg" statement)
updates.whatIsNew: Prospective randomised open-label blinded-endpoint trial, 39 UK stroke centres, Jan 2017-May 2023; 1,858 randomised, 1,777 in the modified ITT population (885 tenecteplase, 892 alteplase). Mean age 70.4 (SD 12.9), median NIHSS 7 (IQR 5-13). Day-90 mRS distribution: OR 1.07 (95% CI 0.90-1.27); P for non-inferiority <0.0001, P = 0.43 for superiority (non-inferiority margin OR 0.75). Deaths 68 (8%) vs 75 (8%); SITS-MOST sICH 20 (2%) vs 15 (2%); PH2 37 (4%) vs 26 (3%); angioedema 6 (1%) in both. The document asserts the tenecteplase dose regimen without citing any tenecteplase-vs-alteplase trial.
updates.citation: Muir KW, Ford GA, Ford I, Wardlaw JM, McConnachie A, Greenlaw N, et al. Tenecteplase versus alteplase for acute stroke within 4·5 h of onset (ATTEST-2): a randomised, parallel group, open-label trial. Lancet Neurol. 2024;23(11):1087-96. doi:10.1016/S1474-4422(24)00377-6.

updates.topic: ORIGINAL — tenecteplase non-inferior to alteplase in Chinese patients within 4.5 h
updates.whatIsNew: Multicentre active-controlled randomised open-label blinded-endpoint non-inferiority trial, 55 Chinese centres, Jul 2021-Jul 2023; 1,489 randomised, 1,465 in the full analysis set (732 tenecteplase, 733 alteplase), 30.4% female, NIHSS 1-25. mRS 0-1 at day 90: 532/732 (72.7%) vs 515/733 (70.3%); RR 1.03 (95% CI 0.97-1.09), non-inferiority margin (RR 0.937) met. sICH (ECASS III) 9 (1.2%) in each group, RR 1.01 (95% CI 0.37-2.70). 90-day mortality 4.6% (34/732) vs 5.8% (43/736); RR 0.80 (95% CI 0.51-1.23).
updates.citation: Meng X, Li S, Dai H, Lu G, Wang W, Che F, et al. Tenecteplase vs alteplase for patients with acute ischemic stroke: the ORIGINAL randomized clinical trial. JAMA. 2024;332(17):1437-45. doi:10.1001/jama.2024.14721.

updates.topic: Extended-window thrombolysis: TRACE-III (positive) vs TIMELESS (neutral) — the document has no extended-window section at all
updates.whatIsNew: TRACE-III (China, 516 patients with ICA/M1 occlusion, salvageable tissue on perfusion imaging, NO access to EVT, randomised 4.5-24 h): mRS 0-1 at 90 d 33.0% tenecteplase vs 24.2% standard care; relative rate 1.37 (95% CI 1.04-1.81), P = 0.03. 90-day mortality 13.3% vs 13.1%; sICH within 36 h 3.0% vs 0.8%. TIMELESS (458 patients, 77.3% subsequently underwent thrombectomy, tenecteplase vs PLACEBO 4.5-24 h): adjusted common OR for 90-day mRS 1.13 (95% CI 0.82-1.57), P = 0.45; 90-day mortality 19.7% vs 18.2%; sICH 3.2% vs 2.3%. The contrast (benefit only where thrombectomy is unavailable) is essential context for any 2026-current chapter on reperfusion.
updates.citation: Xiong Y, Campbell BCV, Schwamm LH, Meng X, Jin A, Parsons MW, et al. Tenecteplase for ischemic stroke at 4.5 to 24 hours without thrombectomy. N Engl J Med. 2024;391(3):203-12. doi:10.1056/NEJMoa2402980. AND Albers GW, Jumaa M, Purdon B, Zaidi SF, Streib C, Shuaib A, et al. Tenecteplase for stroke at 4.5 to 24 hours with perfusion-imaging selection. N Engl J Med. 2024;390(8):701-11. doi:10.1056/NEJMoa2310392.

updates.topic: OPTION — tenecteplase 4.5-24 h in NON-large-vessel-occlusion stroke (the extended-window trial closest to the minor-stroke population)
updates.whatIsNew: Randomised open-label blinded-endpoint trial, 48 Chinese centres, Jun 2023-Aug 2025 (final follow-up 28 Oct 2025); 570 randomised, 566 analysed (median age 68 [IQR 59-75], 196 female [34.6%]), non-LVO stroke with salvageable tissue on perfusion imaging, 4.5-24 h from last seen well. Tenecteplase 0.25 mg/kg (max 25 mg, n=282) vs standard medical treatment (n=284). mRS 0-1 at 90 d: 123/282 (43.6%) vs 97/284 (34.2%); RR 1.28 (95% CI 1.04-1.57), P = 0.02. sICH within 36 h 2.8% vs 0% (risk difference 2.85%, 95% CI 1.16-5.54%, P = 0.004); 90-day mortality 5.0% vs 3.2%, RR 1.57 (95% CI 0.69-3.57), P = 0.28.
updates.citation: Ma G, Mo R, Zuo Y, Ma Q, Zhao G, Yao X, et al. Tenecteplase for acute non-large vessel occlusion 4.5 to 24 hours after ischemic stroke: the OPTION randomized clinical trial. JAMA. 2026;335(13):1137-47. doi:10.1001/jama.2026.0210.

updates.topic: Updated meta-analysis of tenecteplase beyond 4.5 h
updates.whatIsNew: 6 RCTs, 2,297 patients (1,152 tenecteplase, 1,145 best medical treatment without IVT), all treated beyond 4.5 h from last known well. mRS 0-1 at 90 d: OR 1.40 (95% CI 1.18-1.67), P < 0.001; mRS 0-2: OR 1.27 (95% CI 1.07-1.51), P = 0.006; early neurological improvement OR 3.21 (95% CI 1.82-5.66), P < 0.001. sICH increased: OR 2.34 (95% CI 1.11-4.95), P = 0.026. No difference in 90-day mortality (OR 1.17, 95% CI 0.89-1.55), any ICH (OR 1.61, 95% CI 0.37-6.95) or PH2 (OR 1.81, 95% CI 0.90-3.64). PROSPERO CRD420251060492.
updates.citation: Gonçalves OR, Scarcia L, Portela JGS, Santos GSB, Cardoso LJC, da Silva AMP, et al. Tenecteplase beyond the 4.5-h window for patients with acute ischemic stroke: an updated meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials. CNS Drugs. 2026;40(8):1073-87. doi:10.1007/s40263-026-01308-6.

updates.topic: ARAMIS post hoc — the LVO/no-LVO split, and the timing split, for DAPT vs alteplase
updates.whatIsNew: (a) LVO analysis: 480 of 723 ARAMIS patients with a responsible-vessel study; 36 LVO, 444 non-LVO; 20 patients had early neurological deterioration (END, ≥4-point NIHSS rise at 24 h). In the NON-LVO group DAPT beat alteplase for END (adjusted risk difference -4.8%, 95% CI -6.9% to -2.6%, P < 0.001) and for bleeding events (-6.4%, 95% CI -8.9% to -3.9%, P < 0.001); in the LVO group no difference (+2.3%, 95% CI -17.6% to 22.3%, P = 0.82); P for interaction = 0.06. (b) Timing analysis: 719 patients, 362 (50.3%) treated 0-3 h and 357 (49.7%) 3-4.5 h. DAPT gave less END than alteplase at 0-3 h (2.6% vs 10.0%, adjusted P = 0.03) but not at 3-4.5 h (6.8% vs 6.6%, P = 0.79); P for interaction = 0.04. Both refine when DAPT is genuinely the better option.
updates.citation: Cui Y, He C, Li ZA, Wang Y, Chen HS. Dual antiplatelet versus alteplase for early neurologic deterioration in minor stroke with versus without large vessel occlusion: prespecified post hoc analysis of the ARAMIS trial. Stroke. 2024;55(11):2590-8. doi:10.1161/STROKEAHA.124.048248. AND Yao ZG, Pei YF, Chen HS. Onset to treatment time and early neurological deterioration of dual antiplatelet therapy versus alteplase in minor stroke. J Am Heart Assoc. 2025;14(21):e043980. doi:10.1161/JAHA.125.043980.

updates.topic: Countervailing evidence: IVT may help minor stroke WITH large-vessel severe stenosis or occlusion
updates.whatIsNew: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 5 studies (randomised and observational): 1,090 patients with NIHSS ≤5 plus large-vessel severe stenosis or occlusion treated with IVT vs 3,501 with standard medical therapy. IVT improved mRS 0-1 at 90 d (OR 1.58, 95% CI 1.16-2.15); in the LVO subgroup OR 1.52 (95% CI 1.03-2.23). No significant difference in mRS 0-2, sICH, 90-day mortality or 90-day recurrence. PROSPERO CRD42025637459. This is the strongest published counter-argument to a blanket "do not thrombolyse minor stroke" position, and it should be presented against TEMPO-2 (which was randomised and neutral/harmful in this same anatomical population) rather than instead of it.
updates.citation: Zhang T, Tong L, Xu L, Liu R, Xie L, Jiang L, et al. Intravenous thrombolysis versus standard medical therapy in minor stroke patients with large vessel severe stenosis or occlusion: a systematic review and meta-analysis. BMC Med. 2026;24(1):238. doi:10.1186/s12916-026-04777-0.

updates.topic: EAST — early (within 6 h) DAPT after thrombolysis in minor stroke is safe but adds nothing
updates.whatIsNew: Multicentre double-blind placebo-controlled RCT in China, 7 Aug 2022-1 Aug 2024; 1,022 randomised, 995 in the modified ITT analysis (503 early antiplatelet, 492 placebo). Patients had NIHSS 0-5 and had received IV thrombolysis; clopidogrel + aspirin vs placebo started within 6 h after thrombolysis. mRS 0-1 at 90 d: 451/503 (89.7%) vs 441/492 (89.6%); OR 1.00 (95% CI 0.67-1.51), P = 0.99. Safety profiles similar. Directly answers the practical question the document raises (post-thrombolysis antithrombotic timing) and shows the conventional 24-hour wait need not be shortened.
updates.citation: Chen HS, Cui Y, Li XQ, Wang XH, Jiang CH, Li J, et al. Early antiplatelet treatment for minor stroke following thrombolysis: the EAST trial. Eur Heart J. 2026;47(6):746-56. doi:10.1093/eurheartj/ehaf702.

updates.topic: The 2026 AHA/ASA guideline the document leans on has a PUBLISHED CORRECTION and a public dispute — neither is acknowledged
updates.whatIsNew: The guideline itself is confirmed exactly as the document cites it (Stroke. 2026;57(8):e316-e436, doi:10.1161/STR.0000000000000513, PMID 41582814, e-published 26 Jan 2026). However: (1) a formal Correction was published — Stroke. 2026;57(8):e461-e467, doi:10.1161/STR.0000000000000530, PMID 42507797, e-pub 27 Jul 2026; (2) 20 DEFUSE/DAWN investigators (Albers, Warach, Saver, Fisher, Heit, Derdeyn, Lansberg, Schwamm, Muir, Baron and others) formally requested that Recommendation 4.7.2 #2 (EVT for anterior-circulation LVO, ASPECTS ≥6, NIHSS ≥6, 6-24 h) be downgraded from Class 1/LOE A to Class 2b/LOE C-LD; (3) the writing group publicly DECLINED. Verified from the writing group's open-access reply (PMC13491549). The dispute is about EVT imaging selection in the 6-24 h window, NOT about minor-stroke thrombolysis — so it does not undermine the document's lysis statements, but a monograph citing this guideline as settled should note the correction and the live controversy.
updates.citation: Prabhakaran S, Gonzalez NR, Zachrison KS, Adeoye O, Alexandrov AW, Ansari SA, et al. Correction to: 2026 guideline for the early management of patients with acute ischemic stroke: a guideline from the American Heart Association/American Stroke Association. Stroke. 2026;57(8):e461-e467. doi:10.1161/STR.0000000000000530. AND Albers GW, Warach SJ, Saver JL, Fisher M, Heit JJ, Derdeyn CP, et al. Proposed corrections to the 2026 guideline for the early management of patients with acute ischemic stroke. Stroke. 2026;57(9):2935-8. doi:10.1161/STROKEAHA.126.056478. AND Gonzalez NR, Prabhakaran S, Zachrison KS, Leira EC, Bahouth MN, Broderick JP; 2026 AHA/ASA Acute Ischemic Stroke Guideline Writing Group. Response to request for modification of the 2026 AHA/ASA acute ischemic stroke guidelines: endovascular thrombectomy imaging selection in the 6- to 24-hour window. Stroke. 2026;57(9):2939-48. doi:10.1161/STROKEAHA.126.056726.
updates.datePublished: Correction e-pub 2026-07-27; Albers letter and reply e-pub 2026-07-31, issue 2026-09

updates.topic: Current ESO status — no new ESO thrombolysis guideline exists; the document should cite what actually stands
updates.whatIsNew: Exhaustive search of Eur Stroke J 2024 through August 2026 found NO updated ESO guideline on intravenous thrombolysis and none on minor/non-disabling stroke. The standing ESO documents remain the 2021 IVT guideline and the 2023 expedited tenecteplase recommendation. New ESO guidelines published in the window cover other topics (blood pressure 2025 update, intracerebral haemorrhage, basilar artery occlusion 2024, small-vessel disease/lacunar stroke 2024, aphasia, motor rehabilitation, visual impairment, stroke-associated pneumonia, SAH). The document cites only the ESO 2021 TIA guideline and the ESO 2022 secondary-prevention guideline, so its acute-reperfusion sections currently rest on AHA/ASA alone.
updates.citation: Berge E, Whiteley W, Audebert H, De Marchis GM, Fonseca AC, Padiglioni C, et al. European Stroke Organisation (ESO) guidelines on intravenous thrombolysis for acute ischaemic stroke. Eur Stroke J. 2021;6(1):I-LXII. doi:10.1177/2396987321989865. AND Alamowitch S, Turc G, Palaiodimou L, Bivard A, Cameron A, De Marchis GM, et al. European Stroke Organisation (ESO) expedited recommendation on tenecteplase for acute ischaemic stroke. Eur Stroke J. 2023;8(1):8-54. doi:10.1177/23969873221150022.

updates.topic: TEMPO-2 secondary analysis — sex differences
updates.whatIsNew: 884 ITT patients (48.9% tenecteplase, 41.5% female). Among women, tenecteplase was LESS likely to yield return to baseline mRS at 90 d than control (63.8% vs 73.9%; aRR 0.87, 95% CI 0.76-1.00). Among men no difference (77.5% vs 75.4%; aRR 1.03, 95% CI 0.94-1.13). Women randomised to tenecteplase were less likely than men to be responders (63.8% vs 77.5%; aRR 0.85, 95% CI 0.75-0.96). Early recanalisation was more frequent with tenecteplase in both sexes.
updates.citation: Yu AYX, Vatanpour S, Ganesh A, Field TS, Barber PA, Choi PMC, et al. Sex differences in outcomes after tenecteplase for minor stroke: a subanalysis of the TEMPO-2 trial. J Am Heart Assoc. 2025;14(9):e039154. doi:10.1161/JAHA.124.039154.

updates.topic: Long-term prognostic factors after TIA or minor stroke (large 2026 meta-analysis, useful for the monograph's prognosis chapter)
updates.whatIsNew: 28 cohort studies, 86,810 patients with TIA or minor stroke (median age 69, 52-60% male), follow-up ≥1 year, with GRADE certainty and population attributable fractions. High-certainty associations with long-term stroke: age (aHR 1.04/year, 95% CI 1.02-1.05); male sex (1.25, 1.15-1.36); atrial fibrillation (1.34, 1.18-1.52); diabetes (1.52, 1.32-1.75); hypertension (1.60, 1.31-1.94; PAF 19.3%); ischaemic heart disease (1.67, 1.28-2.18); prior stroke/TIA (1.70, 1.43-2.02); smoking (1.29, 1.05-1.60); ABCD2 ≥4 (1.59, 1.31-1.94); acute infarct on imaging (1.97, 1.41-2.74; PAF 19.0%) including DWI-positive lesions (1.86, 1.02-3.37); minor stroke rather than TIA as index event (1.75, 1.35-2.27; PAF 28.0%); aphasia/dysarthria (1.45, 1.24-1.69); paresis (1.45, 1.15-1.84); cardioembolism (2.16, 1.53-3.05); large-artery atherosclerosis (2.19, 1.68-2.86); small-vessel disease (1.69, 1.14-2.49). PROSPERO CRD42023476551.
updates.citation: Khan F, Yogendrakumar V, Lun R, Marx CE, Rochwerg B, Tran A, et al. Prognostic factors for long-term risk of stroke after transient ischemic attack or minor stroke: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Circulation. 2026;153(17):1281-95. doi:10.1161/CIRCULATIONAHA.125.078763.

updates.topic: TRACE-2 — the pivotal tenecteplase non-inferiority trial in a Chinese population (context for the document's dose statement)
updates.whatIsNew: Phase 3 multicentre open-label randomised non-inferiority trial; tenecteplase 0.25 mg/kg vs alteplase 0.9 mg/kg within 4.5 h in patients not eligible for or refusing EVT. Published 2023, so outside the strict 2024-2026 window, but it is the trial pair (with ATTEST-2 and ORIGINAL) that established tenecteplase as an alternative to alteplase, and the document asserts that dose without citing any of them. Multiple 2024-2025 post hoc analyses exist (time-to-treatment, elderly, renal function, diabetes/hyperglycaemia) but NONE is a dedicated minor-stroke subgroup.
updates.citation: Wang Y, Li S, Pan Y, Li H, Parsons MW, Campbell BCV, et al. Tenecteplase versus alteplase in acute ischaemic cerebrovascular events (TRACE-2): a phase 3, multicentre, open-label, randomised controlled, non-inferiority trial. Lancet. 2023;401(10377):645-54. doi:10.1016/S0140-6736(22)02600-9.

7) The CONTENT of Albers et al., "Proposed corrections to the 2026 guideline" (Stroke. 2026;57(9):2935-8, doi:10.1161/STROKEAHA.126.056478, PMID 42535283) could not be read — it is paywalled, has no PubMed abstract, and Semantic Scholar returns a null abstract. Its topic is nevertheless established with certainty from the writing group's open-access reply (PMC13491549), which states the correspondence was signed by 20 DEFUSE/DAWN investigators and requested downgrading Recommendation 4.7.2 #2 (EVT, anterior-circulation LVO, ASPECTS ≥6, NIHSS ≥6, 6-24 h) from Class 1/LOE A to Class 2b/LOE C-LD, and that the writing group declined. It concerns EVT imaging selection, NOT thrombolysis in minor stroke. Do not attribute a minor-stroke position to that letter.

8) WebSearch was unavailable for this session (the 200-call budget was already exhausted before I started), so all verification was done through the NCBI E-utilities (PubMed), Crossref, PMC and Semantic Scholar REST APIs rather than general web search. Everything reported above carries a PMID and/or a Crossref-confirmed DOI with volume, issue and pages; nothing is from memory.

updates.topic: GBD 2021 stroke burden, Vietnam-specific
updates.whatIsNew: The Vietnam-specific GBD 2021 analysis (the document currently has only a GBD 2019-based source). In 2021 stroke caused 166,954 deaths in Vietnam (males 96,764; females 70,190). Age-standardised stroke incidence 203.36 per 100,000 (95% CI 190.51-271.81), higher than Southeast Asia (187.98) and nearly 1.5x the global rate (141.55). Joinpoint AAPC 1990-2021: incidence -0.34%, deaths -0.49%, DALYs -0.61%; prevalence fell in women (AAPC -0.19%) but rose in men (AAPC +0.26%). Metabolic risks were the largest contributor to stroke mortality (144.89 per 100,000) and DALYs (2,872.37 per 100,000); behavioural risks predominated in males, metabolic in females.
updates.citation: Truyen TTTT, Vo NLY, Vo QP, Phan TC, Le PNB, Nguyen HT, et al. Burden and risk factors of stroke in Vietnam from 1990 to 2021 - a systematic analysis from global burden disease 2021. J Stroke Cerebrovasc Dis. 2025;34(3):108241. doi:10.1016/j.jstrokecerebrovasdis.2025.108241.

updates.topic: Extracranial carotid stenosis prevalence in Vietnamese TIA / ischaemic stroke
updates.whatIsNew: First large Vietnamese consecutive-series estimate, and it materially qualifies the document's section 1.3/2 claim that extracranial carotid stenosis causes 15-20% of infarcts. Among 1,191 consecutive TIA/ischaemic stroke patients at Bach Mai Hospital (Jun 2021-Jun 2022), only 62 (5.2%, 95% CI 4.0-6.6) had 50-99% ipsilateral internal carotid stenosis - far below Western figures and comparable to other Asian series. Independent predictors: age OR 1.49 per 10-year increment (95% CI 1.17-1.90, p=0.001); male sex OR 4.94 (95% CI 2.15-11.38, p<0.001); prior stroke OR 2.01 (95% CI 1.12-3.62, p=0.02).
updates.citation: Ton MD, Hung PM, Nguyen TN, Tung BN. Prevalence and associated factors of extracranial carotid stenosis in Northern Vietnamese patients with transient ischemic attack or ischemic stroke. Cerebrovasc Dis Extra. 2025;15(1):210-217. doi:10.1159/000548297.

updates.topic: Early neurological deterioration in Vietnamese minor stroke (NIHSS <=5)
updates.whatIsNew: The single most on-topic Vietnamese study for this monograph, and the document cites nothing like it. 839 patients with NIHSS <=5 admitted within 24 h to Bach Mai Stroke Center (Dec 2023-Aug 2024); END (NIHSS rise >=2 within 72 h) occurred in 88 (10.5%), of which 43.2% within the first 24 h, 35.2% at 24-48 h, 21.6% at 48-72 h. END predicted poor outcome (mRS 2-6): discharge OR 22.76 (95% CI 11.22-46.20, p<0.01), 30 days OR 24.38 (95% CI 14.40-41.29, p<0.01), 90 days OR 21.74 (95% CI 12.63-37.43, p<0.01). Predictors of END: admission NIHSS OR 1.24 (1.03-1.49, p=0.02); SBP >150 mmHg OR 1.70 (1.03-2.81, p=0.04); admission glucose OR 1.07 (1.01-1.14, p=0.02); antiplatelet monotherapy OR 3.69 (2.24-6.08, p<0.01); internal capsule infarct OR 2.54 (1.37-4.71, p<0.01); MCA occlusion OR 3.06 (1.29-7.30, p=0.01); ipsilateral extracranial carotid occlusion OR 4.84 (1.26-18.65, p=0.02); haemorrhagic transformation OR 5.72 (1.07-30.45, p=0.04). Note the antiplatelet-monotherapy signal directly supports the document's DAPT argument in a Vietnamese setting. The published protocol is a separate citable item: Nguyen DT, Mai TD, Dao PV, Ha HT, et al. PLoS One. 2024;19(5):e0302822. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0302822.
updates.citation: Nguyen DT, Mai TD, Dao PV, Ha HT, Fabus M, Fleming M, et al. Early neurological deterioration in patients with minor stroke: a single-center study conducted in Vietnam. PLoS One. 2025;20(5):e0323700. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0323700.

updates.topic: RES-Q registry Vietnam - national scale and secondary-prevention gap
updates.whatIsNew: The concrete Vietnamese RES-Q denominator the document asserts but never quantifies. RES-Q data from 66 hospitals in Vietnam, 2017-2023, comprising 94,144 patients with ischaemic stroke or TIA; 15.1% had atrial fibrillation. AF patients were older, had more heart failure and more severe strokes, and higher in-hospital mortality. Oral anticoagulant use rose from 15.8% pre-admission to 82.4% at discharge, with a shift toward DOACs. The 15.8% pre-admission figure is a directly usable measure of the Vietnamese secondary-prevention gap for the TIA/minor-stroke argument.
updates.citation: Ton MD, Phuong DV, Dung NT, Chi NV, Hoa TT, Minh TC, et al. Anticoagulation patterns in ischemic stroke patients with atrial fibrillation in developing country: insights from the stroke registry in Vietnam. J Cardiovasc Dev Dis. 2024;11(9):269. doi:10.3390/jcdd11090269.

updates.topic: Vietnamese stroke unit network - the only quantitative national organisational data
updates.whatIsNew: The document states (section 1.2.4) that the stroke unit network 'grew rapidly but remains unevenly distributed' with no numbers; this is the national survey that supplies them. 91 eligible hospitals surveyed Nov-Dec 2020, 66 (73%) responded: approximately 70% had a stroke unit; median 630 acute strokes per hospital per year (IQR 250-1,200); >90% used stroke clinical protocols; daytime nurse:patient ratio 1:4; perceived lack of access to psychologists, occupational therapists and speech pathologists; only 50% had a standardised rehabilitation assessment process. Complements ref 21 (Mai DT 2022), which gives the policy history (MOH Circular 47 of 2016 mandating stroke units; ANGELS implemented in 18 stroke-ready hospitals in 2017) but no network counts.
updates.citation: Phan HT, Nguyen TH, Watkins C, Lightbody E, Boaden E, Georgiou R, et al. Organisational survey for acute stroke care in Vietnam: Regional Collaboration Programme. J Stroke Cerebrovasc Dis. 2022;31(11):106792. doi:10.1016/j.jstrokecerebrovasdis.2022.106792.

updates.topic: Intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis prevalence across Asian populations
updates.whatIsNew: The document asserts twice (sections 1.2.4, 1.3.2, 2.4) that ICAS accounts for 30-50% of infarcts in East Asians, sourced only to CICAS (2014, Chinese). This 2025 systematic scoping review of 142 studies shows the true picture is far more heterogeneous: reported ICAS prevalence ranged 3% to 89.4% (median 13%), and frequency among ischaemic stroke patients ranged 7.9% to 82.4% (median 41.65%). 54 studies reported prevalence, 56 frequency in ischaemic stroke, 120 risk factors; most were from China, Hong Kong, Korea and Japan, with MR and transcranial ultrasound the commonest modalities and >=50% the usual stenosis threshold. The authors explicitly attribute the spread to non-standardised imaging criteria. The document's '30-50%' sits inside this range but should be presented as a median-with-wide-heterogeneity figure rather than a fixed proportion.
updates.citation: Navarro JC, Pedregosa BIC, Punsalan MTS, Baroque GAB, Sarfati MSF, Cañete MTA, et al. Intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis in Asia: a systematic scoping and rapid review of prevalence, frequency in ischaemic stroke and risk factors. BMJ Neurol Open. 2025;7(2):e001164. doi:10.1136/bmjno-2025-001164.

updates.topic: Intracranial atherosclerosis in an ethnically Vietnamese population
updates.whatIsNew: The closest thing that exists to a Vietnamese ICAS prevalence figure, and it strongly supports the document's central premise. Ten-year retrospective analysis (2011-2020) of Vietnamese-born versus Australian-born residents of South-Western Sydney: intracranial atherosclerotic disease 30.9% vs 6.9% (p<0.001) and intracerebral haemorrhage 24.7% vs 14.4% (p=0.002) in Vietnamese-born patients. Risk profile differed: hypertension 83.7% vs 70.3% (p<0.001) and dyslipidaemia 81.0% vs 68.2% (p<0.001) higher, but ischaemic heart disease 10.4% vs 20.3%, smoking 24.4% vs 40.8% and alcohol abuse 9.6% vs 15.9% lower (all p<0.001). Predictors of ICAD in Vietnamese patients: diabetes OR 1.86 (95% CI 1.14-3.04, p=0.014); HbA1c OR 1.51 (95% CI 1.15-1.98, p=0.003). Caveat for the monograph: this is a diaspora cohort in Australia, not an in-country Vietnamese cohort.
updates.citation: Alysha D, Blair C, Thomas P, Pham T, Nguyen T, Cordato TR, et al. Comparative prevalence of cerebrovascular disease in Vietnamese communities in South-Western Sydney. J Cardiovasc Dev Dis. 2024;11(6):164. doi:10.3390/jcdd11060164.

updates.topic: Atrial fibrillation prevalence in Vietnamese TIA / ischaemic stroke
updates.whatIsNew: Cross-sectional study of 2,038 consecutive TIA or ischaemic stroke patients at Bach Mai Hospital: AF prevalence 18.1% (95% CI 16.46-19.85), which the authors note exceeds rates reported in other Southeast Asian countries. Adjusted associations: valvular heart disease aOR 9.59 (95% CI 7.10-12.95); age per 10 years aOR 1.39 (95% CI 1.23-1.57); eGFR decrease per 10 mL/min/1.73 m2 aOR 1.12 (95% CI 1.06-1.17); ejection fraction <50% aOR 2.61 (95% CI 1.62-4.21). The very high VHD odds ratio is a Vietnam-specific aetiological point (rheumatic valve disease) that Western-derived cardioembolic workup algorithms in the document do not capture.
updates.citation: Phong PD, Tung BN, Hung PM, Quang NN, Hoai NTT, Dung NV, et al. Prevalence and factors associated with atrial fibrillation in patients with transient ischemic attack or ischemic stroke in Northern Vietnam. J Clin Med. 2023;12(17):5516. doi:10.3390/jcm12175516.

updates.topic: International RES-Q benchmarking of acute stroke care quality
updates.whatIsNew: The largest RES-Q cross-sectional analysis published, and the benchmark the document's Vietnamese health-system argument should be measured against. 334,184 patients from 1,130 hospitals in 70 countries; 218,832 (65.5%) from 47 countries had acute ischaemic stroke. Between-country variation: EMS use 7-97%; stroke unit/ICU admission 12-100%; median door-to-imaging 7-41 min; median door-to-needle 20-75 min; IV thrombolysis rates from <1% to 52%. Higher hospital volume correlated with more SU/ICU admission and shorter times (Spearman rho = 0.10, -0.22 and -0.42 respectively). Vietnam contributes through People's Hospital 115, Ho Chi Minh City (co-author Nguyen Huy Thang).
updates.citation: Mikulik R, Neto G, Sedani R, Ameriso SF, Mammadova N, Marchenko S, et al. Differences in acute ischemic stroke treatment: a cross-sectional study from international Registry of Stroke Care Quality (RES-Q). Int J Stroke. 2026;21(2):188-199. doi:10.1177/17474930251364082.

updates.topic: GBD 2023 global stroke figures (supersede GBD 2021 headline numbers)
updates.whatIsNew: GBD has moved to 2023 estimates since the document's ref 29 (GBD 2021, Lancet Neurol 2024). In 2023 there were 13.2 million incident strokes, 104.8 million people living with stroke, 6.8 million stroke deaths and 156.5 million DALYs; stroke was the second leading cause of death and third leading cause of death and disability combined. Ischaemic stroke was 63.9% of incident cases; over 80% of stroke deaths and DALYs occurred in low- and middle-income countries; 83% of global stroke burden was attributable to 24 modifiable risk factors, led by high systolic blood pressure, with high ambient temperature, obesity and lead exposure rising most since 1990. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: this is online ahead of print with no volume or final page numbers assigned, so it cannot yet be cited with volume/pages. It also does not give Vietnam-level figures - for those, use the Truyen 2025 GBD 2021 paper above.
updates.citation: Feigin VL, Volovici V, Brainin M, Norrving B, Martins SO, Roth GA. The latest global stroke fact sheet 1990-2023: Global Burden of Disease Study. Neuroepidemiology. 2026 May 7:1-18. doi:10.1159/000552065. [Online ahead of print - no volume/issue/final pages assigned as of 29 Aug 2026.]

updates.topic: Stroke subtype distribution in Vietnam - TOAST profile
updates.whatIsNew: A point that cuts against the document's framing and should be addressed rather than ignored. In this review of Asian hospital-based registries, large artery atherosclerosis predominates among ischaemic strokes in China, India, Indonesia, Japan, Pakistan and Korea, but small artery occlusion predominates in Vietnam (as in Bangladesh, Nepal, Singapore, Sri Lanka, Taiwan and Thailand), with cardioembolism third. Combined with the Ton 2025 finding of only 5.2% significant extracranial carotid stenosis, this suggests the Vietnamese TIA/minor-stroke population may be more small-vessel-dominant than the document's large-artery-atherosclerosis emphasis implies. Hypertension is the commonest risk factor across Asia, diabetes usually second.
updates.citation: Venketasubramanian N. Stroke epidemiology in Asia. Cerebrovasc Dis Extra. 2025;15(1):81-92. doi:10.1159/000543399.

updates.topic: Timing of carotid stenting after TIA / non-disabling stroke in Vietnam
updates.whatIsNew: Direct Vietnamese evidence for the document's carotid revascularisation timing discussion (chapter 3), which currently rests entirely on NASCET/ECST/CREST. Prospective observational cohort of 71 patients with symptomatic extracranial ICA stenosis undergoing carotid stenting at Bach Mai, Jan 2022-Dec 2024; mean age 70.5 +/- 8.6 years, 90.1% male. Early CAS (<=14 days, n=42) versus delayed (15-90 days, n=29): 30-day stroke/death 7.14% vs 6.90% (p=1.00); overall 7.04%. Median time to revascularisation 11 days overall (early 7.5 days, IQR 5-10; delayed 30 days, IQR 30-40; p<0.01). Recurrent ischaemic events: 42.3% had >=1 event in the 90 days before CAS, falling to 7.0% at 0-30 days and 1.4% at 31-90 days after CAS (p<0.001). Small single-centre cohort - report as feasibility evidence, not as a comparative-effectiveness result.
updates.citation: Nguyen Tung B, Quoc Thai N, Manh Hung P, Ngoc Quang N, Huynh Linh D, Duy Ton M. Timing of extracranial carotid revascularization following ischemic stroke or TIA: outcomes of early carotid stenting in a cohort study. Medicine (Baltimore). 2026;105(10):e47748. doi:10.1097/MD.0000000000047748.

updates.topic: Existing ref 34 (Tran MC 2025) - numbers the document omits, plus a GBD-vintage caveat
updates.whatIsNew: The document cites this at section 1.2.4 but states no figures. The paper reports: RES-Q Vietnam 2017-2023 comprised 95,696 ischaemic strokes (77%), 23,203 intracerebral haemorrhages (18%) and 2,816 subarachnoid haemorrhages (2%); Vietnam had among the highest stroke incidence and prevalence in Southeast Asia and ranked 4th in stroke mortality of 11 neighbouring countries; GBD 2019 stroke incidence 222 per 100,000 (95% UI 206-242) and prevalence 1,541 per 100,000 (1,430-1,679), with 135,999 stroke deaths; city-level RES-Q rates Hanoi incidence 168.9 / prevalence 1,182.2 and Ho Chi Minh City incidence 207.1 / prevalence 1,221.8; leading attributable risks were high systolic blood pressure (79,000 deaths), diet (43,000), high fasting plasma glucose (35,000) and air pollution (33,000). CAVEAT the document should state explicitly: the burden half of this paper uses GBD 2019, not GBD 2021 - so citing it alongside ref 29 (GBD 2021) for the same claim mixes two GBD cycles. Pair it with Truyen 2025 for GBD 2021 Vietnam figures.
updates.citation: Tran MC, Prisco L, Pham PM, Phan HQ, Ganau M, Pham N, et al. Comprehensive analysis of stroke epidemiology in Vietnam: insights from GBD 1990-2019 and RES-Q 2017-2023. Glob Epidemiol. 2025;9:100199. doi:10.1016/j.gloepi.2025.100199.

updates.topic: Existing ref 21 (Mai DT 2022) - published correction not cited
updates.whatIsNew: The reference itself is correct (Stroke Vasc Interv Neurol. 2022;2(2):e000331, published 8 Mar 2022) and supplies the policy timeline the document uses: MOH Circular 47 (2016) mandating construction of stroke units, and the ANGELS programme implemented in 18 stroke-ready hospitals in 2017. However PubMed records a published correction that the document does not cite.
updates.citation: Correction to: Current state of stroke care in Vietnam. Stroke Vasc Interv Neurol. 2022;3(3):e12306. doi:10.1161/svi2.12306.

updates.topic: Existing ref 5 (2026 AHA/ASA acute ischaemic stroke guideline) - published correction not cited
updates.whatIsNew: The document's ref 5 is CONFIRMED accurate exactly as written: Stroke. 2026 Aug;57(8):e316-e436, doi:10.1161/STR.0000000000000513, PMID 41582814. A correction was published in the same issue and is not cited in the document.
updates.citation: Correction to: 2026 guideline for the early management of patients with acute ischemic stroke: a guideline from the American Heart Association/American Stroke Association. Stroke. 2026;57(8):e461-e467. doi:10.1161/STR.0000000000000530.

updates.topic: Asian consensus and Chinese national guidance on intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis
updates.whatIsNew: Two 2026 documents relevant to the document's chapter 3 ICAS management section. (1) The first Chinese national guideline dedicated to ICAS diagnosis and treatment - useful as a regionally-derived counterpart to SAMMPRIS/CASSISS-based recommendations, but note it is online ahead of print with no volume or pages assigned. (2) A modified-Delphi protocol for Asian consensus recommendations on standardised ICAS diagnosis and imaging (Navarro JC, Pedregosa BC 2nd, Belen AA, Gan RN, et al. BMJ Open. 2026;16(3):e112266. doi:10.1136/bmjopen-2025-112266) - this is a PROTOCOL only; the consensus recommendations themselves are not yet published as of 29 Aug 2026.
updates.citation: Leng X, Sui B, Liu C, Wang T, et al. Chinese guidelines for diagnosis and treatment of intracranial atherosclerotic stenosis. Int J Stroke. 2026 Jan 22:17474930261419812. doi:10.1177/17474930261419812. [Online ahead of print - no volume/pages assigned.]
